title: Sufficiency of Scripture
definition: The sufficiency of Scripture means that God's written Word contains all He intends His people to have as the final authority for salvation, doctrine, correction, godliness, and faithful obedience.
summary: The church may use helps, teachers, and tools, but no resource stands above or beside Scripture as a higher rule of faith and life.
christFocus: The sufficiency of Scripture rests in the sufficiency of Christ, whom Scripture faithfully reveals as Savior, Lord, and Shepherd.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: Sufficiency of Scripture teaches that God's people must receive this truth under the authority of the Lord, allowing Scripture itself to define the doctrine rather than personal opinion, tradition, or culture.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This doctrine matters because it protects the believer from confusion and helps the church remain anchored in what God has actually spoken. Without this truth, faith can drift toward feelings, assumptions, or human wisdom.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: A disciple should respond to sufficiency of scripture by reading the Word prayerfully, testing beliefs by Scripture, obeying what God reveals, and helping others handle the Bible with humility, clarity, and faith.

studySections.heading: Guardrails and Common Errors
studySections.content: This doctrine should not be used to win arguments while neglecting love, nor should it be separated from prayer, obedience, and dependence on the Holy Spirit. The goal is faithful submission to God, not mere possession of information.
